sources.note: The post itself states no prosodic fact; it promises that 'All words and phrases in the grammar will be tone marked, and there will be a complete account of tone' and lists a Phonological Sketch (3.1 Consonants, 3.2 Vowels, 3.3 Tones, 3.4 Reduplication). Its reference list cites Collins 1993 Topics in Ewe Syntax (MIT diss., Kpele data) and Clements 1978 'Tone and syntax in Ewe' -- standard-Ewe/Kpele sources, none on Kpessi.

sources.note: No phonology content. Kpessi occurs only as a name in the synoptic inventory tables (Tableau 1 Takassi 1983, Tableaux 2A/2B Aféli 2003, Tableau 3 Grimes 2009); it is absent from Tableau 4 (Gblem-Poidi & Kantchoa 2012, 37 parlers incl. evegbe/gengbe). The words ton/tonal/accent do not occur; 'phonétique/phonologie' appears once in the proposed survey methodology (sec. 3.1.1.2). Useful only as evidence that Togolese inventories list Kpessi separately while Gblem-Poidi & Kantchoa fold it into Ewe.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2005. A synchronic lexical study of Gbe language varieties: the effects of different similarity judgment criteria. Linguistic Discovery 3(1): 22-53. Dartmouth College Library. doi:10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.281
sources.note: No phonology content: lexicostatistical methodology (Gudschinsky/Blair similarity criteria, two criteria sets WLC1/WLC2, MDS and clustering) and percentage matrices; Kpesi appears only in cluster memberships and similarity figures (e.g. lowest similarity with Wance/Wundi, 71-72%). 'stress' occurs only as Kruskal's MDS stress; 'tone', 'tonal', 'accent', 'pitch' do not occur. No word-list forms are printed, so not even tone-marked data for Kpesi.

sources.citation: Westermann, Diedrich. 1907. Grammatik der Ewe-Sprache. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. Sec. 58 'Starkton', p. 38.
sources.note: Ewe generally (ewee1241, Anlo-based standard), NOT Kpési: the first high tone of a sentence or compound (or, absent a high tone, the first mid/low) sounds somewhat stronger, 'rein physiologisch'; 'die Ewesprache auch im Satz keine Betonung kennt, die sich nach dem Inhalt des Gesprochenen richtet' -- i.e. no content-based stress, only fixed syllable tones. Context only for this key.
